title: Multi-language tool invocation bridge, fingerprint validators, and ergonomic streaming wrappers
creator: Asha Kumar
description:
Problem: Client SDKs for Python/TypeScript/Go currently provide ad-hoc helpers for function/tool calling but differ in validation behavior, retry semantics, and streaming ergonomics. This causes inconsistent developer experience and subtle production bugs (duplicate tool invocations, lost stream offsets, or poorly surfaced schema errors).

Goal: Implement a small, language-idiomatic invocation bridge plus a fingerprint-based schema validator and a set of ergonomic streaming wrappers that: (1) unify validation errors across SDKs, (2) provide resumable / backpressured streaming adapters, and (3) expose deterministic retry primitives (idempotency + non-idempotent fallbacks). Deliver cross-language examples and unit/integration tests demonstrating migration paths for existing callers.
acceptance_criteria: SDKs expose a stable invocation_bridge API in Python/TS/Go that standardizes function schema validation and invocation lifecycle
A fingerprint validator computes and caches a compact schema fingerprint, rejects mismatches with actionable errors, and logs telemetry events
Streaming wrappers support pause/resume + checkpoint tokens so long-running tool streams can be resumed after transient failures
Retry policy primitives include: idempotency token propagation, per-call max-retries, and a configurable non-idempotent fallback policy
Cross-language example repository with 3 examples: sync tool call, streaming tool call with resume, and mixed sync/async orchestration
Unit tests and integration tests cover validation failures, retry edge-cases, and stream resume behaviour
Backward-compatible for existing SDK users (opt-in feature flag during rollout)
technical_notes: Fingerprint validator: SHA-256 over a canonicalized schema (sorted keys, stable type names) encoded as base64; store fingerprint in per-user cache with TTL; compare server-provided schema fingerprint to prevent schema drift.

Invocation bridge responsibilities: schema validation, idempotency token generation and propagation, telemetry hooks (validation_failed, invocation_retry, stream_resume), and canonical error mapping to SDK error types.

Streaming adapters: Python -> async generator that yields (chunk, checkpoint_token), TS -> AsyncIterable with resume(checkpoint) helper, Go -> channel + ResumeToken struct. ResumeToken is an opaque string from server combining offset + invocation fingerprint.

Retries: Exponential backoff with jitter. For non-idempotent calls use a two-phase strategy: optimistic retry if safe-to-retry header present, otherwise surface explicit RetryableNonIdempotentError with guidance to user.
Observability: emit structured logs and metric tags: sdk.lang, invocation.key, fingerprint.match = {true,false}, retry.reason, stream.resume_count.

Trade-offs: Strong validation reduces silent failures but can block gradual schema evolution; we provide a feature-flaged "lenient_validation" option and a migration tool that accepts a server-side 'compatibility-mode' token for rollout.
Security: fingerprints reveal schema fingerprints only; do not transmit full schema in telemetry. Confirmed with Security that fingerprint + TTL cache is acceptable (low risk).
implementation_plan: Phase 1: PoC (1 week): implement fingerprinting lib in Python and TS, add unit tests for canonicalization and collision checks
Phase 2: Bridge core (2 weeks): implement invocation_bridge in Python/TS/Go with schema checks, idempotency token, and basic retry primitives
Phase 3: Streaming ergonomics (2 weeks): implement async generator/AsyncIterable/channel adapters + checkpoint token flow; add integration tests against runtime staging server
Phase 4: Examples + docs (1 week): add cross-language examples, docblocks, and migration guide. Coordinate with docs team for SDK release notes
Phase 5: Rollout (1 week): feature flag default off, run dogfood apps, flip flag for internal orgs, monitor telemetry, then broader rollout
testing_plan: Unit tests: fingerprint canonicalization, validation error mapping, idempotency token generation, backoff calculations
Integration tests: simulate server schema drift, assert validator blocks incompatible invocations, assert resume tokens rehydrate stream position
Load test: high concurrency invocation_bridge throughputs to ensure fingerprint cache reduces validation overhead (target: < 2% P50 overhead)
System test: run example orchestration with flaky network (kill connections) and assert streams resume within SLA and no duplicate non-idempotent side-effects when idempotency token absent
Manual QA: UX review of error messages and docs for actionable remediation steps

2025-02-20 - Liam O'Neill: Implemented TS fingerprint lib and wired basic validation. Initial PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/4821 opened for review.
2025-02-22 - Security (review): fingerprint-only telemetry OK. Recommended adding TTL and opt-out flag. Marked security_review_required=false.

2025-02-25 - Eng Infra: suggested using local LRU cache shared by worker processes rather than per-request redis to keep validation overhead < 1ms. We will prototype with an in-process LRU and measure.

2025-02-28 - Design review (Maria Chen): asked for clearer error copy when schema drift occurs; suggested showing 'expected fingerprint' + 'observed fingerprint' and a link to migration guide. Added to docs scope.
2025-03-01 - Liam O'Neill: Added streaming resume token format proposal to PR. Using compact Base64(op+offset+fingerprintSlice) to keep token short. Need UX review on opaque token visibility in logs.

2025-03-02 - QA: added flaky-network integration test that simulates mid-stream disconnects. Current implementation successfully resumes in 94% of runs; target 99% — follow-up to tune retry/backoff and checkpoint frequency.
